topic: Eight NVIDIA DGX Sparks clustered into 1 TB of unified memory running the GLM 5.3 753B frontier model
title: 8 DGX Sparks, 1 TB: frontier AI on a desk
description: Working description; the package stage overwrites this. Eight DGX Sparks now cluster into 1 TB of unified memory and run the full GLM 5.3 (753B) at about 470 GB in NVFP4. You'll learn what the cluster really buys: capacity, not speed. (Narration is AI-generated.)
hook_candidates: One terabyte of memory, on your desk.
Eight desk boxes now hold what a datacenter rents.
NVIDIA just blessed an eight-Spark cluster.
Your desk just got a terabyte of model memory.
A frontier model now runs on eight desk boxes.
Eight Sparks, one terabyte, one cable.
Eight DGX Sparks replaced the datacenter rental.
The four hundred seventy gigabyte file on a desk.
Eight little boxes, one frontier model, no cloud.
narration_full: Eight DGX Sparks pool one terabyte of memory. They are desk boxes. A terabyte meant a building you rent. GLM five point three runs across all eight. Seven hundred fifty-three billion parameters. Squeezed to four bits a weight: about four hundred seventy gigabytes of model. NVIDIA measured thirty-one tokens per second for one user. That is how fast the model writes: about reading speed. The catch is the cable. A Spark's own memory outruns its ConnectX seven link, the cable between boxes, eleven times over. Eight boxes buy room, not speed. So the biggest models stopped being rentals. A frontier checkpoint now runs on your desk.

One text block animating at a time.

On 'about reading speed' the cursor stops and the line dims. Number is on screen exactly while spoken.
